sources.title: Anomalous U(1) extension of the Standard Model

evidence.text: Can explicit anomaly-free SM × U(1)A models yield an apparently anomalous low-energy Z′ theory after heavy chiral fermions are integrated out, with calculable three-vector interactions and a perturbatively controlled separation of vector and fermion masses?

sources.title: Anomaly free gauged R symmetry in local supersymmetry

evidence.text: Can a gauged R-symmetry provide an anomaly-free supergravity extension of the supersymmetric Standard Model, with viable symmetry breaking and restrictions on baryon- and lepton-number violation?

sources.title: Anomalous U(1) extension of the Standard Model

evidence.text: The effective action is split into kinetic, axionic and GCS pieces. Their gauge variations are combined with the anomalous one-loop triangle variation; demanding vanishing total variation fixes the effective coefficients in terms of anomaly traces and gauge couplings.

sources.title: Anomaly free gauged R symmetry in local supersymmetry

evidence.text: Combines superpotential charge constraints with mixed gauge, cubic R, and gravitational anomaly equations; separates a singlet-independent subsystem, then uses algebraic solutions and bounded numerical scans for singlet charges.

sources.title: Anomalous U(1) extension of the Standard Model

evidence.text: Gauge invariance of SM and secluded Yukawa couplings constrains charges. The authors then solve gauge and mixed gauge–gravitational anomaly equations, requiring opposite nonzero contributions from the two sectors. They construct selected rational solutions rather than classify all possibilities.

sources.title: Anomalous U(1) extension of the Standard Model

evidence.text: One-loop gauge running is matched across a common heavy threshold Mf. The resulting estimates constrain fermion multiplicities and gA under different perturbativity targets. The heavy threshold is also compared with tree-level and anomaly-induced contributions to the Z′ mass.

sources.title: Anomaly free gauged R symmetry in local supersymmetry

evidence.text: Uses superconformal compensator transformations and a field redefinition to express gauged R-supergravity in canonical supergravity form. Homogeneity of the superpotential produces the constant contribution to the R-multiplet D-term.

sources.title: Topological Origin of Chiral Symmetry Breaking in QCD and in Gravity

evidence.text: Does nonzero vacuum topological susceptibility before adding massless fermions suffice to require dynamical breaking of the full anomalous chiral flavor symmetry, a massive axial pseudo-Goldstone and elimination of massless fermions, without assuming confinement?

sources.title: Nonanomalous discrete R symmetry and light gravitino

evidence.text: Can nonanomalous discrete R symmetries generate µ ≃ 1 TeV from fractional powers of the superpotential VEV when the gravitino is lighter than the weak scale, while sufficiently suppressing baryon- and lepton-number violation?

sources.title: Implications of the weak gravity conjecture in anomalous quiver gauge theories

evidence.text: A light scalar supplies attractive Yukawa exchange between charged fermions, allowing gauge and scalar strengths to be compared after anomaly cancellation.

sources.title: Longlived superheavy dark matter with discrete gauge symmetries

evidence.text: Can anomaly-free discrete gauge symmetries give superheavy dark-matter particles lifetimes of approximately 10^10–10^22 years in supersymmetric models with neutrino masses, and what additional structures evade the minimal-model obstruction?

sources.title: Proton stability: From the standard model to beyond grand unification

sources.title: Flavor 'conservation' and hierarchy in TeV scale supersymmetric standard model

sources.title: Spontaneous <math display="inline"><mi>C</mi><mi>P</mi></math> violation and flavor changing neutral currents in minimal SO(10)

evidence.text: Can spontaneous CP violation in minimal nonsupersymmetric SO(10) require observable electroweak scalars and yield discriminating relations among flavor violation and proton-decay branching ratios?

sources.title: Phenomenology of non-Abelian gauge and Goldstone bosons in a U(2) flavor model

evidence.text: Can the previously unexamined SU(2)F bosons of a realistic U(2)F flavor model provide distinctive experimental tests through flavor-changing meson and lepton processes, for either global or gauged SU(2)F?

sources.title: Fermion mass hierarchy and a high quality axion from gauged U (1) flavor symmetry

evidence.text: Can an anomaly-free gauged flavor symmetry explain fermion hierarchies while producing an accidental PQ symmetry whose axion survives gravitational corrections, supplies dark matter, and accompanies successful leptogenesis?

sources.title: Towards the Swampland of Flavour Symmetries

evidence.text: Can flavour theories without explicit symmetry protection suppress light-family transitions while remaining predictive and testable, with flavour parameters emerging from infrared dynamics?

sources.title: A Lot of flavor physics from a little symmetry

evidence.text: Can a small spontaneously broken discrete gauged flavor symmetry accommodate charged-fermion hierarchies, large atmospheric neutrino mixing and either historical solar MSW solution, while controlling supersymmetric flavor-changing neutral currents?

sources.title: Gauged L(mu) - L(tau) with large muon anomalous magnetic moment and the bimaximal mixing of neutrinos

evidence.text: Can electroweak-scale gauged Lμ−Lτ explain the possible positive muon anomalous-moment discrepancy, accommodate nearly bimaximal neutrino mixing, and yield observable collider signatures?

sources.title: Natural R parity, $\mu$-term, and fermion mass hierarchy from discrete gauge symmetries

evidence.text: Can a discrete gauge symmetry simultaneously protect MSSM R parity, forbid a bare μ term while allowing Giudice–Masiero generation, and explain fermion mass and mixing hierarchies?

sources.title: Hidden symmetries and their implications for particle physics

evidence.text: How can discrete gauge symmetries protect otherwise vulnerable low-energy selection rules and address baryon violation, R-parity, neutrino masses, the supersymmetric μ problem, flavor hierarchies, and axion stability?

sources.title: More about discrete gauge anomalies

evidence.text: How do heavy fermions, discrete Green–Schwarz cancellation, and gauged R-symmetries modify discrete anomaly constraints and the symmetries available for suppressing flavour-changing neutral currents and proton decay?

sources.title: SUSY SU(6) GIFT for doublet-triplet splitting and fermion masses

evidence.text: Can a supersymmetric SU(6) model with flavour-blind discrete symmetry simultaneously realize Goldstone Higgs doublets, μ of the soft-breaking scale, and hierarchical fermion masses and mixing without a horizontal symmetry?

sources.title: Anomalous U(1)'s and proton stability in brane models

evidence.text: Can a family-independent anomalous U(1), canceled through a brane generalized Green–Schwarz mechanism, suppress MSSM proton-decay operators and the μ-term while permitting viable fermion masses?

sources.title: D-branes and the standard model

evidence.text: Which restricted type-I D-brane embeddings can realize Standard Model charges at a low string scale while preserving proton stability, protecting small neutrino masses, reproducing gauge couplings, and generating acceptable heaviest-generation masses and neutrino oscillation patterns?

sources.title: TeV scale supersymmetric standard model and brane world

evidence.text: Can the low-unification-scale TSSM protect proton stability and small neutrino masses through anomaly-free gauge symmetries, while preserving its unification prediction and yielding distinctive phenomenology?

sources.title: Flavor 'conservation' and hierarchy in TeV scale supersymmetric standard model

evidence.text: Can anomaly-free flavor gauge symmetries suppress FCNCs in the low-string-scale TSSM while preserving its proton-stability and neutrino-mass protections, particularly with two large transverse dimensions?

sources.title: A Novel string derived Z-prime with stable proton, light-neutrinos and R-parity violation

evidence.text: Replace specified parent-operator fields by their VEVs, preserve all cutoff powers, and impose the quoted coefficient limits. The output is conditional on both the integer insertion orders and the existence of the required charged fields.

sources.title: Proton Stability and Light $Z^\prime$ Inspired by String Derived Models

evidence.text: Review boundary-condition basis vectors, modular-invariance restrictions, generalized GSO projections, and world-sheet fermion charges to explain how different SO(10)-breaking patterns produce different U(1)ζ charge signs.

sources.title: Lepton Mixing Parameters from Discrete and CP Symmetries

evidence.text: Enumerate S4 choices of residual generators and compatible CP transformations, reduce equivalent choices by group similarity transformations, and examine all row/column permutations. Historical mixing-angle fits are assessed with χ² functions.

sources.title: Supersymmetric $SU(5) \times U(1)_\chi$ and the weak gravity conjecture

evidence.text: Gauge couplings are evolved at two loops with SARAH. The paper also presents two-loop b and τ Yukawa running, including finite one-loop bottom-Yukawa threshold corrections in selected supersymmetric examples.

sources.title: Anomalies and accidental symmetries: charging the scalar leptoquark under L$_{\mu}$ − L$_{\tau}$

evidence.text: Compute finite scalar mass corrections and estimate radiatively generated portal couplings using one-loop beta functions, βλ=dλ/d ln μ², with tree-level portals taken small. Inserting the induced Higgs–leptoquark quartic into a one-loop mass correction estimates an anomaly-dependent two-loop contribution; a separate electroweak two-loop correction is included.

sources.title: Electroweak flavour unification

evidence.text: Local anomaly counting is supplemented by an Atiyah–Hirzebruch spectral-sequence computation of spin bordism, using characteristic classes and a Steenrod-square differential to identify possible global gauge anomalies.

sources.title: Theory and phenomenology of Dirac neutrinos

evidence.text: How can symmetry-protected seesaw and radiative mechanisms explain small Dirac neutrino masses while connecting neutrino nature to dark matter stability, flavour predictions and observable charged lepton flavour violation?

sources.title: Anomaly free gauged R symmetry in local supersymmetry

evidence.text: Can a gauged R-symmetry provide an anomaly-free supergravity extension of the supersymmetric Standard Model, with viable symmetry breaking and restrictions on baryon- and lepton-number violation?

sources.title: Lepton flavor violation from SUSY with non-universal scalars

evidence.text: How do scalar non-universality, neutrino Yukawa mixing and electroweak naturalness affect LFV predictions and experimental reach in NUHM3 with a supersymmetric type-I seesaw?

sources.title: Horizontal gauge symmetry and masses of neutrinos

evidence.text: The three-family extension places all displayed leptons in horizontal triplets so that family symmetry can organize neutrino and charged-lepton interactions within one gauge setting.

sources.title: The dark dimension and the Swampland

evidence.text: Can inferred high-scale gauge unification and proton stability coexist with a substantially lower higher-dimensional Planck scale?

sources.title: Nonanomalous discrete R symmetry and light gravitino

evidence.text: Can nonanomalous discrete R symmetries generate µ ≃ 1 TeV from fractional powers of the superpotential VEV when the gravitino is lighter than the weak scale, while sufficiently suppressing baryon- and lepton-number violation?

sources.title: Longlived superheavy dark matter with discrete gauge symmetries

evidence.text: Can anomaly-free discrete gauge symmetries give superheavy dark-matter particles lifetimes of approximately 10^10–10^22 years in supersymmetric models with neutrino masses, and what additional structures evade the minimal-model obstruction?

sources.title: TASI Lectures on Remnants from the String Landscape

evidence.text: What precision and collider signatures follow when another gauged SU(2) acts on right-chiral fermions?

sources.title: Pseudo-Goldstone Neutrinos and Majoron Phenomenology from Spontaneous $U(1){Lμ-L_τ}$ Breaking

evidence.text: Can spontaneous global U(1)Lμ−Lτ breaking in a supersymmetric model generate realistic neutrino masses through a pseudo-Goldstone RH neutrino while correlating Majoron interactions, invisible neutrino decay and heavy-neutrino signatures?

sources.title: A Novel string derived Z-prime with stable proton, light-neutrinos and R-parity violation

evidence.text: Can the extra proton-protecting U(1) coexist with light active neutrinos? The neutral singlets and heavy-singlet Higgs VEV provide operators that preserve the residual gauge symmetry while generating a seesaw mass matrix.

sources.title: Supersymmetric alignment models for (g − 2)$_{μ}$

evidence.text: Can supersymmetric flavor alignment with horizontal U(1) symmetries and spontaneous CP violation accommodate the reported muon magnetic-moment anomaly while suppressing flavor violation and electric dipole moments?

sources.title: Revisiting the Number-Theory Dark Matter Scenario and the Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Can anomaly-required chiral fermions yield a long-lived dark matter particle alongside an ultralight stable fermion, with the latter removing the neutrino-scale AdS minimum of the circle-compactified Standard Model?

sources.title: Spontaneous CP violation and horizontal symmetry in the MSSM: toward lepton flavor naturalness

evidence.text: Can horizontal flavor symmetry and exclusively spontaneous CP violation make lighter MSSM superpartners compatible with leptonic flavor and EDM limits, and how should unknown O(1) mass-matrix coefficients enter a measure of flavor naturalness?

sources.title: Anomalous U(1) extension of the Standard Model

evidence.text: Can explicit anomaly-free SM × U(1)A models yield an apparently anomalous low-energy Z′ theory after heavy chiral fermions are integrated out, with calculable three-vector interactions and a perturbatively controlled separation of vector and fermion masses?

sources.title: Horizontal gauge symmetry and masses of neutrinos

evidence.text: The reviewed models ask whether a local family symmetry can connect electronic and muonic matter while keeping induced flavour-changing interactions sufficiently weak.

sources.title: Discrete symmetries and isosinglet quarks in low-energy supersymmetry

evidence.text: Can weak-isosinglet quarks have low or intermediate masses without causing rapid proton decay, protected by a family-independent, anomaly-consistent discrete gauge symmetry?

sources.title: Embedding cosmological inflation, axion dark matter and seesaw mechanism in a 3-3-1 gauge model

evidence.text: Can a nonsupersymmetric 3-3-1 model use one complex scalar singlet to connect radiatively corrected inflation, an invisible axion and type-I seesaw neutrino masses?

sources.title: Minimal family unification

evidence.text: What economical gauged nonabelian family symmetry can distinguish the heavy third family and organize lighter masses while satisfying anomaly cancellation and adding no new quarks?

sources.title: Advances in old fashioned heterotic string model building

evidence.text: What progress in perturbative heterotic model building was reported around SUSY ’97, particularly concerning proton stability, anomalous U(1)s, observable–hidden kinetic mixing, and realistic gauge and matter constructions?

sources.title: Further swampland constraint on Dirac neutrino

evidence.text: Can anomaly-free U(1) twists of circle-compactified Standard Model fields, together with the non-SUSY AdS or AdS distance conjecture, further constrain Dirac neutrino masses and the surviving B−L symmetry?

sources.title: A Novel string derived Z-prime with stable proton, light-neutrinos and R-parity violation

evidence.text: Can a low-energy Abelian gauge symmetry protect the proton without obstructing fermion masses or a neutrino seesaw? The proposed symmetry must also be family universal and anomaly free.

sources.title: Simple nonAbelian finite flavor groups and fermion masses

evidence.text: Which small nonabelian finite family groups can be gauged consistently and organize a top-dominated fermion hierarchy through sequential symmetry breaking and radiative masses, with no additional quarks and minimal extra leptons?
